legacy_root.answer: Four production parsers were fed a known-good document and the same document plus extra field '__tst0052_unknown__'. All four REJECT the unknown field with an error that names it: plugin.json -> PluginManifestError: plugin.json rejected unknown field __tst0052_unknown__: '__tst0052_unknown__' does not match any of the regexes: '^x-'; install-handoff -> HandoffValidationError: Additional properties are not allowed ('__tst0052_unknown__' was unexpected); exec-policy -> ValidationError: Additional properties are not allowed ('__tst0052_unknown__' was unexpected); hooks.json -> LoadRefusal: hooks.json rejected unknown field __tst0052_unknown__: extra top-level key(s) '__tst0052_unknown__' are not allowed (permitted: hooks, version). All four ACCEPT the unmodified known-good document (test_known_field_still_accepted). No production parser on this worktree silently accepts unknown top-level fields. The json.loads negative control DOES accept the extra key and retains 'this-value-must-not-be-applied' on the dict; named getters never read it, which is what a lenient client would do with the ignored value. .claude-plugin/plugin.json present=True (fixtures used). SUCCESS:TST-0052

lenient_control.ignored_value_fate: json.loads retained the extra key on the dict (__tst0052_unknown__='this-value-must-not-be-applied'); named getters (name, version, permissions, hooks) never read it, so the client applies the known fields and silently ignores the value
lenient_control.parser: json.loads (negative control; not a production parser)
